title: New Believer
subtitle: For those who just met Jesus

lessons.title: Who Is God?
lessons.verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
teaching: God is the Creator who made the whole world, and He exists eternally of Himself. We are creatures He has made, and in Him we find true life and the meaning of life.
God is love, and He is holy and righteous. He is one God, yet exists in three persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (the Trinity).
This God is not far off; He is a Father who calls us as His children and longs to meet us personally.
The Westminster Shorter Catechism Q.1 teaches: “Man’s chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him forever.” We were made to know and glorify this very God.

questions.question: Who is God?
options: The Creator who made the world
questions.explanation: God is the Creator who made the heavens and the earth (Gen 1:1).

questions.question: How does the one God exist?
options: As three persons — Father, Son, Spirit
questions.explanation: One God in three persons is called the Trinity.

questions.question: How does God want to relate to us?
options: As a Father who calls us His children
questions.explanation: He wants to make us His children and meet us personally.

questions.question: In how many days did God create the world?
questions.explanation: God created the heavens and earth in six days.

questions.question: What is man’s chief end? (Catechism Q.1)
options: To glorify God and enjoy Him forever
questions.explanation: This is the teaching of Shorter Catechism Q.1.

questions.question: How many Gods are there?
questions.explanation: The living and true God is only one.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three persons of God?
questions.explanation: The three persons are the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Which correctly describes God’s character?
questions.explanation: God is love, holy, and righteous.

questions.question: What are people in relation to God?
questions.explanation: We are creatures God has made.

questions.question: Where is God?
questions.explanation: God is infinite and is everywhere.

lessons.title: What Kind of Book Is the Bible?
lessons.verse: All Scripture is God-breathed.
teaching: The Bible is ‘the Word of God,’ which God had people write down. It has 39 books in the Old Testament and 27 in the New — 66 books in all.
The Bible tells us who God is, salvation through Jesus, and how we ought to live.
So Christians steadily read and hear the Bible and live according to its Word.

questions.question: What kind of book is the Bible?
questions.explanation: The Bible is the Word of God, written by God’s inspiration.

questions.question: How many books are in the Bible total?
questions.explanation: OT 39 + NT 27 = 66 books.

questions.question: What is the core message of the Bible?
questions.explanation: The center of the Bible is salvation through Jesus Christ.

questions.question: How many books are in the Old Testament?
questions.explanation: The Old Testament has 39 books.

questions.question: How many books are in the New Testament?
questions.explanation: The New Testament has 27 books.

questions.question: By whose inspiration was the Bible written?
questions.explanation: All Scripture is God-breathed (2 Tim 3:16).

questions.question: What is the first book of the Bible?
questions.explanation: The first book is Genesis.

questions.question: What is the last book of the Bible?
questions.explanation: The last book is Revelation.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the Gospels recording Jesus’ life?
questions.explanation: The Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.

questions.question: What is the right attitude toward the Bible?
options: Read it steadily and follow it
questions.explanation: We steadily read the Word and live by it.

lessons.title: Human Sin and God’s Love
lessons.verse: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
teaching: People turn away from God, live by their own will, and sin. Sin blocks the way between God and us, and its result is death.
Yet God loved us sinners and sent His one and only Son, Jesus, opening the way of salvation.
Admitting our sin and returning to God is the very beginning of salvation.

questions.question: What do all people have in common, according to the Bible?
questions.explanation: All have sinned (Rom 3:23).

questions.question: What is the result of sin?
options: Separation from God, leading to death
questions.explanation: The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23).

questions.question: What is God’s heart toward sinners?
options: He opens the way of salvation in love
questions.explanation: God loved us and sent Jesus.

questions.question: Through whom did sin first enter the world?
questions.explanation: Sin entered through the disobedience of the first humans, Adam and Eve.

questions.question: In ‘The wages of sin is ___’ (Rom 6:23), what fills the blank?
questions.explanation: The wages of sin is death (Rom 6:23).

questions.question: Sin blocks the way between us and what?
questions.explanation: Sin blocks the way between God and us.

questions.question: Is everyone a sinner?
questions.explanation: All have sinned (Rom 3:23).

questions.question: What is the beginning of salvation?
options: Admitting sin and returning to God
questions.explanation: Repentance — admitting sin and turning back — is the beginning.

questions.question: Whom did God send to save sinners?
options: His one and only Son, Jesus
questions.explanation: God sent His one and only Son, Jesus (John 3:16).

questions.question: God hates sin, but how does He treat the sinner?
options: He loves them and opens salvation
questions.explanation: He hates the sin but loves the sinner.

lessons.title: Jesus Christ and Salvation
lessons.verse: For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son,
teaching: Jesus is the Son of God. He came as a man, died on the cross in our place for our sins, and rose again on the third day.
We receive forgiveness of sins and eternal life as a gift — not by good works but by faith in Jesus. This is grace.
Whoever believes in and receives Jesus as Savior and Lord becomes a child of God.

questions.question: Why did Jesus die on the cross?
options: To bear our sins in our place
questions.explanation: Jesus died bearing our sins in our place.

questions.question: How are we saved?
questions.explanation: Salvation is God’s gift received by faith (Eph 2:8).

questions.question: What does one who believes and receives Jesus become?
questions.explanation: To those who receive Him He gives the right to become children of God (John 1:12).

questions.question: Whose Son is Jesus?
questions.explanation: Jesus is the Son of God.

questions.question: How many days after His death did Jesus rise?
questions.explanation: He rose on the third day (1 Cor 15:4).

questions.question: On what basis are we saved?
questions.explanation: Salvation is by grace, through faith (Eph 2:8).

questions.question: What is it called that Jesus came as a man?
questions.explanation: God becoming man is called the Incarnation.

questions.question: What is the event of Jesus rising again called?
questions.explanation: Conquering death and living again is called the Resurrection.

questions.question: How is salvation received?
questions.explanation: We are saved only by faith in Jesus.

questions.question: What gift is given to those who believe in Jesus?
options: Forgiveness of sins and eternal life
questions.explanation: He gives forgiveness of sins and eternal life as a gift.

lessons.title: What Is Baptism?
lessons.verse: Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them …
teaching: Baptism is a sacred rite that publicly confesses and confirms that one has believed in Jesus and become His own.
The water symbolizes the washing away of sin and new life. Baptism signifies that, united with Christ, our old self dies and we live again as a new person.
Baptism does not ‘create’ salvation. It is a means of grace that confirms — as a sign and a seal — the salvation already received by faith.

Our denomination (the Presbyterian Church, Hapdong) baptizes not only those who confess faith themselves but also believers’ children (infant baptism), because the children too are ‘covenant children’ within God’s covenant.

questions.question: What is the meaning of baptism?
options: A public confession that one belongs to Christ
questions.explanation: Baptism is a rite that publicly confesses belonging to Christ.

questions.question: What does the water of baptism symbolize?
options: The washing of sin and new life
questions.explanation: The water symbolizes the washing of sin and new life.

questions.question: Does baptism create salvation?
options: No, it confirms salvation received by faith
questions.explanation: Baptism is a sign and seal confirming the salvation received by faith.

questions.question: In whose name is baptism received?
options: The Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: It is received in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19).

questions.question: Union with whom does baptism signify?
questions.explanation: It signifies dying and rising again in union with Christ.

questions.question: What is the baptism given to believers’ children called?
questions.explanation: It is infant baptism given to covenant children (Hapdong).

questions.question: What does the Hapdong church call believers’ children?
questions.explanation: Believers’ children are covenant children within God’s covenant.

questions.question: With what is baptism received?
questions.explanation: It is received through washing with water.

questions.question: What does the water of baptism NOT symbolize?
questions.explanation: The water symbolizes washing of sin, new life, and purity (not wealth).

questions.question: For adults, what must precede baptism?
options: A confession of faith in Christ
questions.explanation: Baptism follows a confession of faith and obedience.

lessons.title: Repentance and Faith
lessons.verse: Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.
teaching: Repentance is turning from sin and changing the direction of heart and life toward God.
Faith is trusting that Jesus is my Savior and entrusting myself entirely to Him.
Repentance and faith are both a one-time decision and a lifelong attitude of life.

questions.question: What is repentance?
options: Turning from sin back to God
questions.explanation: Repentance is not mere regret but a change of direction.

questions.question: What is faith?
questions.explanation: Faith is trusting and entrusting oneself.

questions.question: How long do repentance and faith last?
questions.explanation: Repentance and faith are a lifelong walk.

questions.question: In ‘Repent, for the ___ has come near’ (Matt 4:17), the blank is?
questions.explanation: He said to repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.

questions.question: What accompanies true repentance?
questions.explanation: Repentance changes direction and leads to a changed life.

questions.question: Who is the object of faith?
questions.explanation: Faith trusts and relies on Jesus Christ.

questions.question: By what are we justified?
questions.explanation: We are justified by faith alone (justification by faith).

questions.question: Repentance turns from what to what?
options: From the church to the world
questions.explanation: It is turning from sin toward God.

questions.question: Is faith merely knowing?
options: No, it is trusting and entrusting
questions.explanation: True faith trusts and entrusts oneself.

questions.question: What is the right attitude when we fall into sin again?
options: Repent and come to the Lord again
questions.explanation: We repent and come again to the Lord.

lessons.title: Assurance of Salvation
lessons.verse: … so that you may know that you have eternal life.
teaching: Assurance of salvation rests not on my feelings but on God’s promise (His Word).
God has clearly promised eternal life to those who believe in Jesus.
Therefore, even when our hearts waver, we hold to the promise of the Word and enjoy peace.

questions.question: What is the basis of assurance of salvation?
questions.explanation: Assurance rests not on changing feelings but on the unchanging Word.

questions.question: What has God given to those who believe in Jesus?
questions.explanation: He has given eternal life to believers (1 John 5:13).

questions.question: When feelings waver, what do we do?
options: Hold to the promise of the Word
questions.explanation: When we hold to the promise, we enjoy peace.

questions.question: On what is assurance of salvation based?
questions.explanation: Assurance rests on the unchanging Word.

questions.question: What has God promised believers?
questions.explanation: He has given eternal life to believers (1 John 5:13).

questions.question: Is salvation maintained by my works?
questions.explanation: God holds and preserves us to the end.

questions.question: Which is a wrong basis that shakes assurance?
questions.explanation: Changing feelings are not a basis for assurance.

questions.question: Who gives the status of ‘child of God’?
questions.explanation: God has made us His children.

questions.question: What is the life of one who has assurance of salvation?
questions.explanation: Assurance leads to a life of peace and gratitude.

questions.question: What happens to the saved person in the end?
questions.explanation: The saints are preserved to the end (kept by God).

lessons.title: The Christian Life and Communion
lessons.verse: … do this in remembrance of me.
teaching: The saved person obeys God with thankfulness and grows ever more like Jesus (sanctification).
Faith grows through worship, prayer, the Word, fellowship, and service. Faith grows not alone but within the community of the church.
Communion (the Lord’s Supper) is a rite in which, with bread and cup, we remember Jesus’ cross and engrave its grace on our hearts.

questions.question: What is the life of a saved person?
options: Obeying in thankfulness and growing like Jesus
questions.explanation: As fruit of salvation, we live a sanctified life.

questions.question: Which is NOT a channel for faith to grow?
questions.explanation: Faith grows together within community.

questions.question: What is the meaning of Communion (the Lord’s Supper)?
questions.explanation: Communion is a rite remembering the Lord’s death.

questions.question: What is it called when a saved person grows more like Jesus?
questions.explanation: Growing in holiness to become like Jesus is called sanctification.

questions.question: Which is NOT a channel for faith to grow?
questions.explanation: Faith grows through worship, prayer, the Word, and fellowship.

questions.question: What is used in Communion?
questions.explanation: With bread and cup we remember the Lord’s body and blood.

questions.question: What does Communion remember?
questions.explanation: It remembers the Lord’s death (Luke 22:19).

questions.question: What is needed to partake of Communion worthily?
questions.explanation: We examine ourselves and partake with discernment (1 Cor 11:28).

questions.question: How should a Christian worship?
questions.explanation: We worship wholeheartedly, thankful for the grace of salvation.

questions.question: Where does faith grow together?
questions.explanation: Faith grows together within the church community.

lessons.title: What Is Confirmation?
lessons.verse: Everyone ought to examine themselves, and then … eat and drink.
teaching: Confirmation is when a person who was baptized as an infant, or who confesses faith, now personally and publicly confesses their own faith and becomes a full member of the church.
A confirmed member partakes in Communion and shares the rights and duties of the church.
In particular, a covenant child baptized as an infant grows up and, by personally confessing faith, is confirmed and becomes a baptized member (full member).
Confirmation is not a mere formality but a confession of faith resolving to follow the Lord for life.

questions.question: What is confirmation?
options: Personally confessing faith and becoming a full member
questions.explanation: Confirmation is a public confession of faith and becoming a full member.

questions.question: What does a confirmed member come to partake in?
questions.explanation: After confirmation, one partakes in Communion.

questions.question: What is the essence of confirmation?
options: A confession to follow the Lord for life
questions.explanation: Confirmation is a resolve and confession of faith.

questions.question: What is done publicly for confirmation?
questions.explanation: One publicly confesses one’s own faith.

questions.question: What does one baptized as an infant do upon growing up?
questions.explanation: A covenant child grows up and is confirmed.

questions.question: What does a confirmed baptized member have?
options: The rights and duties of the church
questions.explanation: They bear both the rights and duties of the church.

questions.question: Which Scripture says ‘examine yourself’?
questions.explanation: We are told to examine ourselves before Communion (1 Cor 11:28).

questions.question: Whose decision is confirmation?
questions.explanation: It is one’s own personal confession of faith.

questions.question: What does a confirmed person become in the church?
questions.explanation: Through confirmation one becomes a full member (baptized member).

questions.question: What is the right attitude in confirmation?
options: A resolve to follow the Lord for life
questions.explanation: It is a resolve of faith to follow the Lord for life.

lessons.title: The Apostles’ Creed — What We Believe
lessons.verse: If you declare with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” … you will be saved.
teaching: The Apostles’ Creed is a confession summarizing the core truths Christians believe.
It confesses the Father’s creation, the Son Jesus’ redemption, the Holy Spirit’s sanctifying work, and the church, the forgiveness of sins, and eternal life.

This confession is the faith held not by me alone but by the whole church together. Presbyterian churches, including Hapdong, take the Apostles’ Creed together with the Westminster Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms as the standard for faith and life.

questions.question: What is the Apostles’ Creed?
options: A summary confession of the core truths we believe
questions.explanation: The Apostles’ Creed is a confession summarizing the core of faith.

questions.question: Which triune God does the Apostles’ Creed confess?
questions.explanation: It confesses the triune God — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

questions.question: Whose faith is the Apostles’ Creed?
options: The faith the whole church has believed together
questions.explanation: It is the faith of the universal church, confessed together.

questions.question: Who is the object of the first confession in the Apostles’ Creed?
options: God the Father almighty, maker of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: We first confess God the Father, the Creator.

questions.question: Which is NOT an event of Jesus confessed in the Apostles’ Creed?
questions.explanation: The Bible does not teach reincarnation.

questions.question: Which is NOT a doctrinal standard of the Hapdong church?
questions.explanation: Presbyterian churches follow the Westminster Standards.

questions.question: If you confess Jesus as Lord with your mouth and believe in your heart? (Rom 10:9)
questions.explanation: He promised that you will be saved (Rom 10:9).

questions.question: After the Holy Spirit, which is NOT confessed in the Apostles’ Creed?
questions.explanation: We confess the church, forgiveness of sins, and eternal life (not reincarnation).

questions.question: What of faith is the Apostles’ Creed?
options: A summary confession of core truths
questions.explanation: It is a confession summarizing the core truths we believe.

questions.question: In how many persons does the God we believe exist?
questions.explanation: He is the triune God.

lessons.title: The Ten Commandments — God’s Law
lessons.verse: You shall have no other gods before me.
teaching: The Ten Commandments are a standard for life that contains God’s will: to love God (commandments 1–4) and to love your neighbor (commandments 5–10).
We are not saved by keeping the Ten Commandments; rather, as those already saved, we obey with thankfulness.
Jesus summarized all these commandments as ‘love for God and love for neighbor.’

questions.question: What are the two great themes of the Ten Commandments?
options: Love for God and love for neighbor
questions.explanation: Commandments 1–4 are love for God; 5–10 are love for neighbor.

questions.question: Why do we keep the Ten Commandments?
options: As the saved, obeying in thankfulness
questions.explanation: It is not a condition for salvation but a response of thankfulness.

questions.question: What is the first commandment?
options: You shall have no other gods before me
questions.explanation: The first commandment commands worship of God alone.

questions.question: Which commandments pertain to love for God?
questions.explanation: Commandments 1–4 are love for God.

questions.question: Which commandments pertain to love for neighbor?
questions.explanation: Commandments 5–10 are love for neighbor.

questions.question: ‘Honor your father and mother’ is which commandment?
questions.explanation: It is the fifth commandment.

questions.question: ‘You shall not murder’ is which commandment?
questions.explanation: It is the sixth commandment.

questions.question: How did Jesus summarize the Ten Commandments?
options: Love for God and love for neighbor
questions.explanation: He summarized it as love for God and love for neighbor.

questions.question: When do we keep the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: Not a condition for salvation but a response of thankfulness.

questions.question: Where is the moral law summarized?
questions.explanation: The moral law is summarized in the Ten Commandments (Shorter Catechism Q.41).

lessons.title: The Lord’s Prayer and the Life of a Church Member
lessons.verse: This, then, is how you should pray:
teaching: The Lord’s Prayer is the model of prayer Jesus Himself taught, seeking both God’s glory and our needs.
A confirmed member devotes themselves to Sunday worship, lives by the Word and prayer, and serves the church through service, evangelism, and giving.
Faith grows not alone but together within the community of the church.

questions.question: Who taught the Lord’s Prayer?
questions.explanation: It is the prayer Jesus Himself taught (Matt 6:9).

questions.question: What does the Lord’s Prayer seek together?
questions.explanation: It seeks both God’s kingdom and our needs.

questions.question: Which is NOT part of a confirmed member’s life?
questions.explanation: Faith grows by serving within community.

questions.question: How does the Lord’s Prayer begin?
questions.explanation: It begins with “Our Father in heaven.”

questions.question: What does the Lord’s Prayer seek first?
questions.explanation: It seeks God’s glory first.

questions.question: What does ‘Give us today our daily bread’ ask for?
questions.explanation: We rightly ask for what we need in this life.

questions.question: What does the Lord’s Prayer teach about forgiveness?
options: Forgiveness of our sins and forgiving others
questions.explanation: As those forgiven, we forgive others.

questions.question: What should a confirmed member be devoted to?
questions.explanation: We devote ourselves to worship, the Word, and prayer.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to serve the church?
questions.explanation: We serve through service, evangelism, and giving.

questions.question: Where does faith grow together?
questions.explanation: Faith grows within community.

title: Deeper Bible Study
subtitle: Discipleship to know Jesus more deeply (I–V)

lessons.label: Session 1
lessons.title: The Start of a New Life
lessons.verse: if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come … the new is here!
teaching: Having believed in and received Jesus, you are now a ‘new creation.’ The old life has passed, and a new life has begun as a child of God.
This “Deeper Bible Study” is a journey to know Jesus more deeply and to grow as a disciple who becomes more like Him day by day.
Let us grow one step at a time — not alone, but with the Word and prayer and the brothers and sisters who walk together. Now, shall we begin?

questions.question: What has a person who believes in and receives Jesus become?
questions.explanation: If anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation (2 Cor 5:17).

questions.question: What is the purpose of this course?
options: To know Jesus more deeply and grow as a disciple
questions.explanation: The purpose is to grow as a disciple who knows and resembles Jesus.

questions.question: How does faith grow?
options: Together, in the Word, prayer, and community
questions.explanation: It grows together in the Word, prayer, and community.

questions.question: If we are in Christ, what are we called?
questions.explanation: If anyone is in Christ, they are a new creation (2 Cor 5:17).

questions.question: The old has gone, and what has come?
questions.explanation: Behold, the new has come! (2 Cor 5:17).

questions.question: What should we grow into in this course?
questions.explanation: We grow into a disciple who resembles Jesus.

questions.question: With whom does the new life grow?
questions.explanation: It grows together within community.

questions.question: What is the power for new life?
questions.explanation: It grows by the Word and prayer.

questions.question: What is the status of a person who has believed in Jesus?
questions.explanation: They have become a child of God.

questions.question: Does faith grow all at once?
options: No, it grows one step at a time
questions.explanation: It is a journey of growing one step at a time.

lessons.label: Session 2
lessons.title: Who Is Jesus?
lessons.verse: The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us.
teaching: Jesus came to this earth as fully God and at the same time fully man (the Incarnation). God became man and came among us.
He is the ‘Christ (Messiah)’ — the Savior God promised — and the Son of God.
Because Jesus was entirely without sin, He is the only one who could bear our sins in our place.

questions.question: Who is Jesus?
questions.explanation: Jesus came as true God and true man (the Incarnation).

questions.question: What does ‘Christ’ mean?
questions.explanation: Christ means the Anointed One — the Messiah, the Savior.

questions.question: Did Jesus have any sin?
questions.explanation: Being sinless, He could bear our sins in our place.

questions.question: Being God, what else is Jesus at the same time?
questions.explanation: He is true God and true man.

questions.question: What is it called that God became man and came?
questions.explanation: It is called the Incarnation (John 1:14).

questions.question: In whose body was Jesus conceived and born?
questions.explanation: He was conceived by the Holy Spirit in the virgin Mary.

questions.question: By whose power was Jesus conceived?
questions.explanation: He was conceived by the power of the Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What does ‘Christ’ mean?
questions.explanation: Christ is the Messiah, the Savior.

questions.question: Whose Son is Jesus?
options: The Son of the eternal God
questions.explanation: He is the Son of the eternal God.

questions.question: Why could Jesus bear our sins in our place?
questions.explanation: Only the sinless one can make atonement.

lessons.label: Session 3
lessons.title: What Did Jesus Do?
lessons.verse: Christ died for our sins … and was raised on the third day.
teaching: Jesus bore our sins in our place and died on the cross. He took the punishment we deserved (atonement).
And on the third day after being buried, He conquered death and rose again.
Through this death and resurrection, the relationship between God and us was restored, and whoever believes receives eternal life.

questions.question: What did Jesus do on the cross?
options: Bore our sins in our place
questions.explanation: He took the punishment for our sins in our place (atonement).

questions.question: What happened to Jesus after He died?
options: He rose on the third day
questions.explanation: On the third day He conquered death and rose.

questions.question: What does the resurrection mean?
questions.explanation: The resurrection confirms that He is God and confirms salvation.

questions.question: What is it called that Jesus died on the cross?
questions.explanation: It is the atoning death by which He bore our sins.

questions.question: On what day did Jesus rise?
questions.explanation: He rose again on the third day.

questions.question: What was restored through Jesus’ death and resurrection?
options: The relationship between God and us
questions.explanation: The relationship between God and us was restored.

questions.question: Who took the punishment we deserved?
questions.explanation: Jesus took it in our place.

questions.question: Where is ‘Christ died for our sins’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in 1 Corinthians 15:3-4.

questions.question: What does Jesus’ resurrection prove?
questions.explanation: The resurrection proves His deity and salvation.

questions.question: What does a believer receive?
questions.explanation: The believer receives eternal life.

lessons.label: Session 4
lessons.title: What Is Jesus Doing Now?
lessons.verse: he always lives to intercede for them.
teaching: After His resurrection Jesus ascended into heaven and is now at the right hand of God.
There He continually intercedes (prays) for us, and He sent the promised Holy Spirit to be with us.
And one day He will come again (the Second Coming) and complete all things.

questions.question: Where is Jesus now?
options: At the right hand of God
questions.explanation: He ascended and is at the right hand of God.

questions.question: What is Jesus doing for us now?
questions.explanation: He always lives to intercede for us (Heb 7:25).

questions.question: What will happen to Jesus in the future?
options: He will come again (the Second Coming)
questions.explanation: He will come again and complete all things.

questions.question: Where is Jesus now?
options: At the right hand of God
questions.explanation: He ascended and is at the right hand of God.

questions.question: What is Jesus doing for us now?
questions.explanation: He intercedes for us (Heb 7:25).

questions.question: Where is ‘he always lives to intercede for them’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Hebrews 7:25.

questions.question: Whom did Jesus send to us?
questions.explanation: He sent the promised Holy Spirit.

questions.question: What is it called when Jesus comes again?
questions.explanation: His coming again is called the Second Coming.

questions.question: Where did Jesus go after His resurrection?
questions.explanation: He ascended into heaven (the Ascension).

questions.question: What is our hope?
options: The Lord who will come again
questions.explanation: The Lord who will return is our hope.

lessons.label: Session 5
lessons.title: Believe in Jesus
lessons.verse: to all who received him … he gave the right to become children of God.
teaching: Faith is not merely knowing; it is opening the door of the heart and welcoming Jesus in as my Savior and Lord (receiving Him).
Whoever receives Jesus becomes a child of God and receives eternal life as a gift.
Salvation is not by my effort or goodness but is grace received only through faith in Jesus.

questions.question: What is the ‘faith (receiving)’ the Bible speaks of?
options: Opening the heart’s door to welcome the Lord
questions.explanation: Receiving is welcoming Jesus in as Lord (John 1:12).

questions.question: What does one who receives Jesus become?
questions.explanation: They receive the right to become children of God.

questions.question: How is salvation received?
questions.explanation: Salvation is God’s gift received by faith.

questions.question: Faith opens the heart’s door to welcome whom?
questions.explanation: It is welcoming Jesus in as Lord.

questions.question: What does one who receives Jesus become?
questions.explanation: They become a child of God (John 1:12).

questions.question: Where is ‘to all who received him … the right to become children of God’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in John 1:12.

questions.question: Is faith merely knowing?
options: No, it is receiving and relying
questions.explanation: Faith is receiving and relying on Him.

questions.question: As what must we believe in Jesus?
questions.explanation: We believe in and receive Him as Savior and Lord.

questions.question: Whose gift is salvation?
questions.explanation: Salvation is the gift of God’s grace.

questions.question: What is given to the believer?
options: Forgiveness of sins and eternal life
questions.explanation: He gives forgiveness of sins and eternal life.

lessons.label: Session 6
lessons.title: QT — Time of Fellowship with God
lessons.verse: but whose delight is in the law of the Lord, and who meditates on his law day and night.
teaching: QT (Quiet Time) is a time each day to meet alone with God. We read and meditate on the Word and fellowship in prayer.
The method is simple: ① read the Word → ② meditate on what touches your heart → ③ apply it to your life → ④ resolve in prayer.
Jesus too prayed in a solitary place very early in the morning. The power of QT lies in ‘consistency.’

questions.question: What is QT?
options: A time of fellowship with God in Word and prayer
questions.explanation: It is a daily time to meet God in the Word and prayer.

questions.question: Which is NOT part of the basic flow of QT?
questions.explanation: Read → meditate → apply → pray is the basic flow.

questions.question: What is the most important attitude in QT?
questions.explanation: Consistency is the power of QT.

questions.question: What does QT stand for (in English)?
questions.explanation: Quiet Time — a time to meet quietly with God.

questions.question: Which is the correct basic flow of QT?
questions.explanation: We read, meditate, apply, and pray.

questions.question: How do we handle the Word in QT?
questions.explanation: We read, meditate, and engrave it on the heart.

questions.question: What did Jesus also do?
questions.explanation: He prayed very early in the morning (Mark 1:35).

questions.question: Where is ‘meditates on his law day and night’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Psalm 1:2.

questions.question: With whom do we fellowship through QT?
questions.explanation: It is a time of fellowship with God.

questions.question: What is the fruit of QT?
questions.explanation: We grow closer to God.

lessons.section: III. Assurance of Salvation & God’s Character
lessons.label: Session 7
lessons.title: Assurance of Salvation
lessons.verse: so that you may know that you have eternal life.
teaching: Assurance of salvation rests not on my wavering feelings but on God’s unchanging promise (His Word).
God has clearly said that He gives eternal life to those who believe in Jesus.
Therefore, even when our hearts waver, we hold not to ‘what I feel’ but to ‘what God has promised.’

questions.question: What is the basis of assurance of salvation?
questions.explanation: Assurance rests on the unchanging Word (1 John 5:13).

questions.question: What has God given to the believer?
questions.explanation: He has given eternal life to the believer.

questions.question: On what is assurance NOT based?
questions.explanation: It rests on the Word, not on feelings.

questions.question: What is the basis of assurance of salvation?
questions.explanation: It rests on God’s unchanging promise.

questions.question: What has God promised the believer?
questions.explanation: He has given eternal life to the believer (1 John 5:13).

questions.question: Where is ‘so that you may know that you have eternal life’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in 1 John 5:13.

questions.question: Who holds our salvation fast to the end?
questions.explanation: God holds and preserves us to the end.

questions.question: What is the life of an assured believer?
questions.explanation: Assurance leads to a life of peace and gratitude.

questions.question: What do we hold when our hearts waver?
questions.explanation: We hold to the promise of the Word.

questions.question: What is good about having assurance of salvation?
questions.explanation: Assurance gives a bold and thankful life.

lessons.section: III. Assurance of Salvation & God’s Character
lessons.label: Session 8
lessons.title: The Character of God
lessons.verse: The Lord, the compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abounding in love and faithfulness,
teaching: God is love, and at the same time He is holy and righteous. He is also faithful, almighty, and unchanging.
God’s ‘love’ and ‘justice’ met at the cross. He surely judges sin, yet He loved us by having Jesus bear that punishment in our place.
The more we know this God, the more we come to trust and love Him.

questions.question: Which correctly describes God’s character?
options: He is love and is holy and just
questions.explanation: God is love, holy, and righteous.

questions.question: Does God change?
questions.explanation: God is faithful and unchanging.

questions.question: Where did God’s love and justice appear together?
questions.explanation: At the cross, the judgment of justice and love were accomplished together.

questions.question: Does God change?
questions.explanation: God is faithful and unchanging.

questions.question: God is love and also what?
questions.explanation: He is love, holy, and righteous.

questions.question: Where is ‘compassionate and gracious …’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Exodus 34:6.

questions.question: God keeps His promises — that is, He is what?
questions.explanation: God is faithful.

questions.question: What is God’s power like?
questions.explanation: God is almighty.

questions.question: The more we know God, the more we…?
questions.explanation: The more we know, the more we trust and love Him.

questions.question: What does the Bible say God is?
questions.explanation: God is love (1 John 4:8).

lessons.label: Session 9
lessons.title: The Bible
lessons.verse: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful …
teaching: The Bible is the Word of God and the standard for our faith and life.
To make the Word your own, you must hear, read, study, memorize, and meditate on it (like the five fingers).
The Word is food for the soul. We must eat daily for our faith to grow healthy.

questions.question: What is the Bible?
options: The Word of God and the standard for life
questions.explanation: The Bible is the God-breathed Word.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to make the Word your own?
questions.explanation: We receive the Word by hearing, reading, studying, memorizing, and meditating.

questions.question: What is the greatest purpose of the Bible?
options: To lead to salvation and a right life
questions.explanation: The Bible leads us to salvation and a righteous life.

questions.question: Whose word is the Bible?
questions.explanation: The Bible is the Word of God.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to make the Word your own?
questions.explanation: We receive it by hearing, reading, studying, memorizing, and meditating.

questions.question: Where is ‘All Scripture is God-breathed’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in 2 Timothy 3:16.

questions.question: Food for what is the Bible?
questions.explanation: The Word is food for the soul.

questions.question: What is the Word for our life?
questions.explanation: It is the standard for faith and life.

questions.question: After hearing the Word, what should we do?
questions.explanation: We must practice it in life.

questions.question: For healthy faith, the Word should be…?
questions.explanation: We must keep the Word near daily.

lessons.label: Session 10
lessons.title: Prayer
lessons.verse: Do not be anxious about anything, but … by prayer and petition … present your requests to God.
teaching: Prayer is a conversation with God. It is not grand words but speaking honestly, as a child speaks to a father.
Prayer includes thanksgiving and praise, repentance, and petition. We pray in the name of Jesus.
We are told to pray without ceasing. God hears and answers with what is best.

questions.question: What is prayer?
questions.explanation: Prayer is a conversation with God.

questions.question: Which is NOT included in prayer?
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving, praise, repentance, and petition are in prayer.

questions.question: How do we pray?
questions.explanation: We pray without ceasing in the name of Jesus.

questions.question: What is prayer?
questions.explanation: Prayer is a conversation with God.

questions.question: Which is NOT included in prayer?
questions.explanation: Thanksgiving, praise, repentance, and petition are included.

questions.question: Where is ‘Do not be anxious … by prayer and petition’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Philippians 4:6.

questions.question: In whose name do we pray?
questions.explanation: We pray in the name of Jesus.

questions.question: How often do we pray?
questions.explanation: We are told to pray without ceasing (1 Thess 5:17).

questions.question: How does God respond to our prayers?
questions.explanation: He hears and answers with what is best.

questions.question: What is the attitude in prayer?
questions.explanation: We speak honestly, as a child to a father.

lessons.label: Session 11
lessons.title: Fellowship
lessons.verse: not giving up meeting together … but encouraging one another.
teaching: A Christian does not live the faith alone. God has called us into the community of the church.
We worship together, share the Word and prayer, and love, encourage, and serve one another.
Charcoal stays hot when gathered together. When we are diligent to meet, our faith does not grow cold but grows.

questions.question: What is Christian fellowship?
options: Living the faith together as a community
questions.explanation: God has called us into community.

questions.question: How does the Bible say to handle meeting together?
options: Do not give it up, but be diligent
questions.explanation: Do not give up meeting together (Heb 10:25).

questions.question: Which is NOT a picture of fellowship?
questions.explanation: Fellowship is loving and serving together.

questions.question: How does a Christian live the faith?
questions.explanation: We live together as the church community.

questions.question: Where is ‘not giving up meeting together’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Hebrews 10:25.

questions.question: What do we share together?
questions.explanation: We share the Word, prayer, and love.

questions.question: What do we do for one another?
questions.explanation: We love, encourage, and serve one another.

questions.question: To keep faith from growing cold, we should…?
questions.explanation: Faith grows when we are diligent to meet.

questions.question: What is the church?
questions.explanation: The church is a community of believers.

questions.question: Within fellowship, we…?
questions.explanation: We grow together within community.

lessons.label: Session 12
lessons.title: Evangelism
lessons.verse: go and make disciples of all nations,
teaching: Evangelism is sharing with others the gospel I received — that is, Jesus.
This is not the task of special people only but a mission given to every Christian (the Great Commission).
When we set an example by our lives, witness with our words, and rely on the power of the Holy Spirit, the fruit of evangelism comes.

questions.question: What is evangelism?
questions.explanation: Evangelism is sharing the gospel — Jesus.

questions.question: Whose mission is evangelism?
questions.explanation: The Great Commission was given to all believers.

questions.question: What is the true power of evangelism?
questions.explanation: We become witnesses by the power of the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:8).

questions.question: What is evangelism?
questions.explanation: It is sharing the gospel — Jesus.

questions.question: Whose mission is evangelism?
questions.explanation: The Great Commission was given to all believers.

questions.question: Where is ‘make disciples of all nations’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Matthew 28:19.

questions.question: How do we evangelize?
questions.explanation: We witness by the example of our life and our words.

questions.question: Where is ‘you will be my witnesses to the ends of the earth’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Acts 1:8.

questions.question: What are we to share?
questions.explanation: We share the gospel we received — Jesus.

questions.question: Where does evangelism begin?
questions.explanation: Evangelism is sharing the grace we received.

lessons.label: Session 13
lessons.title: A Spirit-Filled Life
lessons.verse: be filled with the Spirit,
teaching: Being filled with the Spirit means fully yielding the control of my life to the Holy Spirit. It is a life in which not I but Christ is king.
When we are governed by the Spirit, the fruit of the Spirit grows: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
Being Spirit-filled is not a one-time event; we must be freshly filled day by day.

questions.question: What does being Spirit-filled mean?
options: Yielding control of life to the Spirit
questions.explanation: It is yielding control to the Spirit, a life Christ rules.

questions.question: Which is NOT a fruit of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: Love, joy, peace, etc. are the fruit of the Spirit (Gal 5:22).

questions.question: How often is being Spirit-filled needed?
questions.explanation: We must be filled day by day.

questions.question: What does being Spirit-filled mean?
questions.explanation: It is yielding control of life to the Spirit.

questions.question: Which is NOT a fruit of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: Love, joy, peace, etc. are the fruit of the Spirit (Gal 5:22).

questions.question: Where is ‘be filled with the Spirit’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Ephesians 5:18.

questions.question: What is the center of a Spirit-filled life?
questions.explanation: It is a life ruled by Christ, not by me.

questions.question: Which is one fruit of the Spirit?
questions.explanation: Patience too is a fruit of the Spirit (Gal 5:22).

questions.question: In a Spirit-filled life, who is king?
questions.explanation: It is a life in which Christ is king.

questions.question: When we are filled with the Spirit, we…?
options: Bear the fruit of the Spirit
questions.explanation: The fruit of the Spirit grows.

lessons.label: Session 14
lessons.title: A Life That Overcomes Temptation
lessons.verse: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to mankind … he will also provide a way out.
teaching: Tests and temptations come to everyone. But God does not allow a temptation we cannot bear, and He always provides a way out.
Jesus too overcame the devil’s temptation with the Word. We also overcome temptation by the Word and prayer.
Even if we fall, we need not despair; we repent, rise again, and come to the Lord.

questions.question: When we are tempted, God…?
questions.explanation: He enables us to bear it and provides a way out.

questions.question: What is the weapon to overcome temptation?
questions.explanation: We overcome by the Word and prayer, as Jesus did.

questions.question: If you fall into sin?
questions.explanation: We repent and come again to the Lord.

questions.question: When we are tempted, God…?
questions.explanation: He enables us to bear it and provides a way out.

questions.question: Where is ‘No temptation has overtaken you …’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in 1 Corinthians 10:13.

questions.question: What is the weapon to overcome temptation?
questions.explanation: We overcome by the Word and prayer.

questions.question: With what did Jesus overcome the devil’s temptation?
questions.explanation: He overcame with the written Word.

questions.question: To whom does temptation come?
questions.explanation: Temptation comes to everyone.

questions.question: What is promised to the one who endures temptation?
questions.explanation: The crown of life is promised (James 1:12).

questions.question: What is our attitude before temptation?
options: Staying alert in the Word and prayer
questions.explanation: We stay alert and resist with the Word and prayer.

lessons.label: Session 15
lessons.title: A Life of Obedience
lessons.verse: If you love me, keep my commands.
teaching: Whoever loves Jesus obeys His Word. Obedience is an expression of love.
God delights in obedience more than in sacrifice. Obedience is not loss but a channel of blessing.
True obedience is done immediately, fully, and with joy.

questions.question: How is love for Jesus expressed?
questions.explanation: If we love Him, we keep His commands (John 14:15).

questions.question: What does God delight in more?
questions.explanation: Obedience is better than sacrifice (1 Sam 15:22).

questions.question: What is the attitude of true obedience?
questions.explanation: It is immediate, full, and joyful obedience.

questions.question: If you love Jesus, what do you do?
questions.explanation: If we love Him, we keep His commands (John 14:15).

questions.question: Where is ‘If you love me, keep my commands’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in John 14:15.

questions.question: What does God delight in more?
questions.explanation: Obedience is better than sacrifice (1 Sam 15:22).

questions.question: Obedience is a channel of what?
questions.explanation: Obedience is a channel of blessing.

questions.question: Obedience is an expression of what?
questions.explanation: Obedience is an expression of love.

questions.question: Whom do we follow in obedience?
questions.explanation: We follow Jesus, who obeyed.

questions.question: What is the heart of an obedient person?
questions.explanation: We obey with joy.

lessons.label: Session 16
lessons.title: A Life of Ministry
lessons.verse: the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom …
teaching: We were not only saved; we were called to serve. God made us for ‘good works.’
We serve the church and our neighbors with the gifts given to each of us. The model of service is Jesus Himself, who came to serve.
And the life of ministry is sharing the grace we received with others, so that a disciple raises up another disciple.

questions.question: What is one purpose for which we were saved?
questions.explanation: We were created for good works (Eph 2:10).

questions.question: In what manner did Jesus come?
questions.explanation: Jesus came to serve and to be a ransom (Mark 10:45).

questions.question: What is the fruit of a life of ministry?
questions.explanation: It is a life where a disciple raises a disciple.

questions.question: For what were we created?
questions.explanation: We were created for good works (Eph 2:10).

questions.question: In what manner did Jesus come?
questions.explanation: He came to serve and to be a ransom (Mark 10:45).

questions.question: Where is ‘the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve’ found?
questions.explanation: It is in Mark 10:45.

questions.question: With what do we serve?
questions.explanation: We serve with the gifts each person received.

questions.question: Whom do we serve?
questions.explanation: We serve the church and our neighbors.

questions.question: Who is the model of service?
questions.explanation: Jesus, who came to serve, is the model.

questions.question: What does a life of ministry ultimately produce?
questions.explanation: It is a life where a disciple raises up a disciple.
